body.statement: Does the following legal same-shell deformation property hold for every nonempty \(\mathcal P_N(s_N)\): there are constants \(c_0,c_1,K>0\), independent of \(N\) and \(s_N\), and laws \(P_0,P_d\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\) obtainable through the handle in \(\operatorname{def:shell-handle}\) such that \(0<|d|\le c_0\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\), \(\|\mu(P_d)-\mu(P_0)\|_\infty\ge c_1|d|\), and \(\operatorname{KL}(P_{0,O}^{N},P_{d,O}^{N})\le KNd^2s_N^2\)?
body.justification: This is the load-bearing open content: algebraic near-null directions yield a minimax converse only after the complete causal experiment and every fixed primitive radius remain legal in the prescribed shell.
body.gap: Yan and Wainwright build instance-wise low-rank lower experiments, while failed prior panel proposals assumed an unspecified interior radius; neither proves shell preservation for the cohort full-law deformation here.
body.consumer: An affirmative answer supplies the premise for all-procedure risk and confidence-width lower bounds; a negative answer requires an explicit quantitative interior-slack restriction before those lower bounds can be asserted.
